name: e-conomic
description: e-conomic — the Danish accounting standard (Visma group): customers, suppliers, booked and draft invoices, products, accounts and journals. REST API, authenticated with two separate tokens.
instructions:
**e-conomic needs two tokens, and they come from different places.**
1. The **App Secret Token** identifies your *application*. You get it once, from e-conomic, when you register as a developer partner at `secure.e-conomic.com/secure/api1/requestaccess.aspx`. It is the same for every customer you connect.
2. The **Agreement Grant Token** identifies the *customer's agreement* (their e-conomic company). The customer grants it by going through e-conomic's app-authorisation URL for your app; each customer produces a different one.
3. Set `ECONOMIC_APP_SECRET_TOKEN` and `ECONOMIC_AGREEMENT_GRANT_TOKEN`.

Both travel as headers on every request — `X-AppSecretToken` and `X-AgreementGrantToken`. A 401 here means one of the two is wrong, and the message does not say which.

**One connector, one agreement.** The grant token binds this connector to one company. A bookkeeper with several clients needs one connector per client.

**Booked vs drafts vs not-due.** e-conomic splits invoices across three collections: `/invoices/drafts` (not yet booked — not revenue), `/invoices/booked` (posted and immutable), `/invoices/not-due` and `/invoices/overdue` (booked and unpaid, split by due date). Summing drafts with booked over-reports; the overdue collection is the direct answer to 'who is late'.

**Paging** is `skippages` and `pagesize` (max 1000). The response's `pagination` block carries `results`, `resultsWithoutFilter` and the link to the next page.

**Filtering** uses e-conomic's own syntax: `filter=date$gte:2026-01-01$and:date$lte:2026-03-31`. Operators are `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$like`, `$in`, joined with `$and:` and `$or:`.

**Cloud reachability**: restapi.e-conomic.com is public with a valid certificate.

tools.name: e_conomic_get_self
tools.description: Read the agreement this connector is bound to: the company name, its CVR number, the application name and the modules enabled. The fastest way to check both tokens at once.

tools.name: e_conomic_list_customers
tools.description: List customers with their number, name, CVR number, address, currency and payment terms.

filter.description: e-conomic filter, e.g. name$like:Muster or customerNumber$gte:1000.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with `-` for descending.

tools.name: e_conomic_get_customer
tools.description: Read one customer by their customer number, with addresses, VAT zone, payment terms and the layout used for their invoices.

tools.name: e_conomic_list_booked_invoices
tools.description: List booked (posted, immutable) invoices with their number, date, due date, customer and totals. This is what 'invoiced revenue' means.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with `-` for descending.

tools.name: e_conomic_get_booked_invoice
tools.description: Read one booked invoice in full: every line with product, quantity, unit price and VAT, plus the totals and the remaining amount.

tools.name: e_conomic_list_overdue_invoices
tools.description: List booked invoices that are past their due date and still unpaid — the direct answer to 'who is late', without needing a filter.

tools.name: e_conomic_list_draft_invoices
tools.description: List unbooked invoice drafts. A draft is not revenue — keep it out of any figure reporting what was actually invoiced.

tools.name: e_conomic_list_suppliers
tools.description: List suppliers with their number, name, CVR number, currency and payment terms, for the purchasing side of the ledger.

tools.name: e_conomic_list_products
tools.description: List products with their number, name, sales price, cost price, unit and the product group they belong to.

tools.name: e_conomic_list_accounts
tools.description: List the chart of accounts with each account's number, name, type, VAT account and current balance.
